Having the data file is not enough to use it correctly. Metadata are needed to interpret variables, units, missing values, QC fields, provenance, and reuse conditions.

### 3. Data Quality and Provenance

Data quality is not simply “good” or “bad”; it depends on the scientific question. Provenance records how data were created and transformed, allowing users to assess whether they are appropriate for a particular use.
